correctness.rationale: Exact finite domain is the 13-point ternary projective plane: two independently implemented, complete Python-standard-library constructions enumerate all 715 candidate four-subsets, identify all 234 ovals, enumerate all 1404 one-point-exchange edges, and run BFS from all 234 starts. Both independently assert every one of 27261 unordered pairs obeys d=4-intersection+1 iff its union is nontrivially blocking, and otherwise d=4-intersection; both check full pair spectrum, uniform sphere profile and exceptional-partner multiplicities. Each executable was inspected and executed successfully. Four-arc counting and degree follow independently from incidence counting; no unbounded-order assertion is made. The proof is a complete finite certificate, not sample-based extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The previously obtained complete ternary smooth-conic pair census already recorded 234 conics and 1638 nontrivially blocking pairs split 702/936; these STATIC counts are credited/excluded from the new contribution. Prior separate 234-state exchange research studies SIX-point minimum nontrivial blockers and a degree-six graph of diameter six, not oval exchanges. Coolsaet--Sticker (2010, full accessible PDF, relevant definitions and auxiliary conic graph examined) classifies arcs; its auxiliary graph is on a different object. Coolsaet--Sticker (2011, author full text) classifies complete arcs in planes of order 27 and 29. Coolsaet--Botteldoorn--Fack (2022, abstract and author page only, full text unavailable) classifies static minimal blocking sets. Targeted published-research searches under projective oval, 4-arc, conic, ternary MDS-code, blocking union and one-point-replacement terms returned no identified dynamic shortest-path theorem covering the exact blocker/detour equivalence. Static pair-orbit data alone does not imply the 234-state exchange distances without an additional geodesic analysis. Residual risk: a historical unindexed treatment or inaccessible full text could encode the same metric.

value.rationale: This is not merely a recomputed oval or blocking-set census: it gives a precise, previously unobserved obstruction to optimal one-point repair of four-point arcs (equivalently projectivized ternary [4,3] MDS generator-column configurations). It determines the complete shortest-path metric, proves that any obstruction causes exactly one extra exchange, identifies the obstruction with natural line-blocking geometry, and counts its occurrence uniformly by shared pairs and individual points. The invariant is a natural local-mobility diagnostic for an extremal, canonical finite configuration space. It does not claim a higher-order theorem or overstate broad impact.
